keyQuestions.text: On a turn where no trigger fires, must the close-out next-steps behaviour still hold?
keyQuestions.answer: Yes for half (A): it must bind on read-only turns, so it belongs in AGENTS.md as a compressed row. No for half (B), which is action-conditioned.

keyQuestions.text: Is the proposal a trigger-shaped cluster or a single row, does an existing rule already carry it, and does it have an AGENTS.md anchor?
keyQuestions.answer: Single row, partly carried by evidence-and-proof §10 and communication §§7-9, anchored by AGENTS.md §10 / §2 / §7 / §8, still refused. Request status: partly satisfied on both halves.

keyQuestions.text: What failure happens today that the absence of this rule caused?
keyQuestions.answer: No failure is evidenced in git history or spec records. The restraint test returns nothing concrete for any net-new rule artifact.

keyQuestions.text: Does the question-tool half sit In or Out of REPO RULES.md §4, and would it be a fourth widening?
keyQuestions.answer: Out, and it would be the fourth widening, of the selection-shaped kind the router pre-refuses. Only an operator decision could widen §4.

keyQuestions.text: Which single shape does the evidence admit: new-rule-file, section-inside-an-existing-rule, AGENTS.md-row or refuse?
keyQuestions.answer: AGENTS.md-row for half (A), decided by the always-loaded test. Refused for any repo-rules artifact: no new rule file, no net-new rule section. Half (B) refused by the scope boundary test.

findings.claim: Gate 5 loads the router on the FIRST write of a session, and read-only turns never fire it.
The router audit measured a read-only turn at 0 rows fired and 0 tokens loaded, while AGENTS.md loads every turn.
The close-out trigger row cannot overcome the Gate 5 read-only exclusion.
Half (A) must hold on read-only turns, where the operator most needs a stated next action.
AGENTS.md already keeps close-out content always loaded and keeps unconditional clauses in §8.
The proposal is a single row, not a trigger-shaped cluster.
evidence-and-proof §10 obliges four status items and what is not done, never an operator action list.
communication §§7-9 oblige verdict-first replies, recommendation shape and consolidated decision-changing questions, never a tool name or action list.
The request is partly satisfied on both halves.
AGENTS.md anchors exist for both halves, so the refusals rest on tests 1 and 2, not on anchor availability.
The four-part test still refuses the ten prior candidates for their recorded reasons.
No incident-level failure caused by the absence of this rule is evidenced in git history or spec records.
findings.evidence: bounded search, coverage named in iteration-003.md

findings.claim: Sub-agent contracts already require next actions at handoff boundaries, and session end routes to a continuation prompt.
With no named failure, the restraint test refuses any net-new rule artifact.
Half (B) sits Out: per-runtime tool naming is ask-surface mechanics, and the posture half is already carried.
Admitting per-runtime tool names would be the fourth widening, of the selection-shaped kind the router pre-refuses.
The third-widening carve-out is not precedent: it admits verification while refusing selection.

verdict.notes: No new rule file and no net-new rule section. Half (B) refused by the scope boundary test, fourth widening is operator-only. Restraint test found no evidenced failure.
